title: Applied labs
description: Build, break, debug and evaluate in your own environment.

lessons.title: Lab: Test-time computation
lessons.conceptOverview: Compare one answer with several sampled candidates plus a deterministic checker. Count total tokens and compare correctness on held-out problems.
lessons.whyItMatters: Evaluate test-time compute, verification and tradeoffs.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Reasoning systems spend inference compute on intermediate computation, alternative candidates or search. Self-consistency aggregates multiple solutions; verification checks candidates using rules, tools or learned judges. Hidden internal reasoning need not be exposed to evaluate an answer; request concise explanations and inspect observable evidence.

sections.title: 1. Establish a baseline
sections.content: Write down your inputs, expected behavior and constraints before starting. Compare one answer with several sampled candidates plus a deterministic checker. Count total tokens and compare correctness on held-out problems.

sections.title: 2. Introduce a failure
sections.content: Test the mistaken assumption: Longer explanations guarantee more reliable answers. Record the observed result and the point where it diverges from your prediction.

sections.title: 3. Debug and evaluate
sections.content: Use the mechanism to explain the failure: Reasoning systems spend inference compute on intermediate computation, alternative candidates or search. Self-consistency aggregates multiple solutions; verification checks candidates using rules, tools or learned judges. Hidden internal reasoning need not be exposed to evaluate an answer; request concise explanations and inspect observable evidence. Change one variable at a time. Repeat the baseline and add a held-out case. Submit the implementation, results and limitations.

commonMistakes: Longer explanations guarantee more reliable answers.
keyTakeaways: Reasoning systems spend inference compute on intermediate computation, alternative candidates or search.

lessons.title: Lab: Supervision, tools & search
lessons.conceptOverview: Create arithmetic tasks with known answers. Compare an unchecked generator, a calculator-assisted solver and a deliberately flawed verifier.
lessons.whyItMatters: Evaluate test-time compute, verification and tradeoffs.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Outcome supervision scores final results; process supervision evaluates intermediate steps. Code execution and symbolic tools can verify calculations, but tools need bounded execution and validated inputs. Search helps only when candidate generation and evaluation are useful; a biased verifier can confidently select wrong answers.

lessons.title: Lab: Reasoning evaluation & routing
lessons.conceptOverview: Plot task success versus total inference budget for factual lookup and multi-step problems. Choose a routing threshold from measurements rather than model reputation.
lessons.whyItMatters: Evaluate test-time compute, verification and tradeoffs.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Evaluate accuracy under a fixed latency and cost budget. Include easy tasks where extra reasoning may increase delay or introduce errors. Route requests using task complexity and measured performance, with a fallback when uncertainty is high. Avoid benchmarks contaminated by training examples.
